messages.content: Respond with three sentences, all containing the same number of characters but using all different words. According to some historians, after the fall of the Western Roman Empire and transition into the Middle Ages, it's said that the Franks contributed the most in defining the Middle Ages as a whole and continued to shape most of Europe up until the end of the Middle Ages. How true is this and what did they do to define the era?

message.content: It is largely true that Frankish political structures, particularly the Carolingian Empire, laid the foundational administrative and cultural groundwork for medieval Europe. By establishing centralized governance, patronizing learning through monastic schools, and forging alliances with the Church, the Franks created a model of Christian kingship that dominated the continent. Their legacy endured because subsequent European kingdoms adopted their legal codes, land systems, and religious institutions, effectively standardizing the era's social fabric.
